interactions.title: Remembering Agata and the ritual
lines: DM: Yeah, all you know about her is that Vola's captors kept mentioning her and saying they were going to take Vola back to her, except they had to wait to make sure the ritual was successful, or make sure the ritual happened before they could return to to Agata. With some suggestion that she, or they, was unusually old for a human, but it was a little unclear.
Wellby: So Agata Dustmother was not the demon doing, like, the scratching-animals ritual that we—
Delwath: Have any evidence that the demon we killed is the one that was summoned, or am I just imagining?
Wellby: We know the water demon that we killed had been summoned, but we don't know by who. Whether it was the other demon, or whether it was Agata, or someone else.

before: Delwath: Ready.
Seeker: Ready. Whoever says it first is the true explanation.
Wellby: Lots of ancient tourist.
DM: They all basically said the same thing. So maybe it's true.
Seeker: It must be true.
after: Kenzo: And also you don't know, like, the weird doppelganger captors of Vola. It's not clear to me what their relationship is with all the other people, like if they're kind of related, on the same team.
Seeker: Where's the doppelganger concept coming from? I'm not clear on what a doppel—what—what is—
Riswynn: In the tower, when we rescued Vola, they—
DM: There were two shape shifters who turned from human normal-looking humans into, like—
Kenzo: Jackal humans, because they were looking for items, looking for items. That's—

interactions.title: Alesh’s expected rendezvous
lines: Delwath: Hold on. One last question. Tim, how much time do we have left till our time for—
DM: ((Timeline lookup and travel estimate)) So—but you have, I would say, maybe, maybe four days, four to five days from Karawa, and maybe seven to 10 before Alesh is expecting you back.
DM: Well, you had originally talked to Alesh that you would meet back in Karawa in like two to three weeks.
Seeker: And hopefully get word about the situation in Tokra with all of the people who fled there.

before: Unknown: Right.
DM: So should we go back in character? I can discuss—
Seeker: I'm glad we were really clarifying a lot of things.
Delwath: So is our next move to return to Karawa?
Seeker: Well, we did fortify the temple there, but we should make sure—
after: Unknown: Right.
Riswynn: I did not meet this Alesh, but Karawa seems like a reasonable place to stop over on my way home, as I was stopping there on my way home. That is still the direction which I imagine heading.
Seeker: We just hope it's not been overrun.
Delwath: And there's still this storm to the west.
Seeker: The storm storm. It does seem worth investigating.

interactions.title: Seeker constructs ley-line goggles
lines: Seeker: I'm making paper maps of all of this, but also you notice I've been making these glass hemispheres. I keep, like, holding them up to my face and looking around, and put them down again. Does appear that there's a line of magical energy heading off in the direction of that storm.
Riswynn: I hear you say, have you crafted something?
Riswynn: Crafted something? I'm not familiar with that sort of glass working.

Seeker: A—it's, it's a work in progress, you see. Mm hmm. I have the ability to visualize the intersection of the plane of magic with this one in the form of the lines we call ley lines that crisscross the landscape. But since not everyone can see them, I thought I might construct a mechanism by which I could share this vision with others.
Seeker: So once I've got the leather strap work together here to make this a set of goggles that might augment the reality that we're—

Seeker: To put them on and you see, there's an interesting principle of the binocular disparity between the field of view of each eye that I can exploit with a magical illusion of small lines on the surface of the glass that, when fused by your mind into a single object, projected out on the landscape in the location of the magical lines.

before: Delwath: And there's still this storm to the west.
Seeker: The storm storm. It does seem worth investigating.

Wellby: Well, Wellby looks up from petting the prairie chicken in his lap and smells the wafting scent of prairie chicken stew and says, “I think we should go there. I think that's where to go next. We lose too much time by going back to Karawa and then coming back again.”
Seeker: Um, Tim, are there—what's the ley lines situation?

DM: Here there are—so Seeker pauses for a moment and sort of concentrates and reaches out his mind, searching for magical lines of energy. And there are, you know, so, so the dwarven stronghold of Raven's Hold, which is a few miles to the—to the east, is a node where three ley lines cross. One of which is—one of which is running west from here, sort of roughly in the direction of—of the storm, one of which is running south roughly towards Karawa, and the other which runs kind of north northeast, north north by northeast a little bit, sort of—and that east by several—sort of like out into the plains, like sort of not in any direction you know.
after: Kenzo: So, what are we doing here? I mean, Wellby, do you want to go towards the crazy electrical storm to hell?
Unknown: Yeah.
Kenzo: Well, there's no covers—like, I mean, it feels like our options are to go there, return to Karawa. Let's do something—
Unknown: Else [garbled]—
Delwath: Think it's worth investigating. I think it's a danger that we leave at our backs otherwise.

Delwath: Wasn't it made to be brought into danger?
Riswynn: Really more of a heritage thing. I mean, it tells stories. What we do when we're at peace, not when we're at war.
Delwath: Wait, is the shield—no, that's not the magic hammer.
Riswynn: Magic hammers very good for dark places, but the shield is—

I think, it's to see to see if we can we can, before we part ways.
Unknown: Yeah.

interactions.title: Remembered teaching from the Karawa priest
lines: Wellby: But we know we know, I thought from from what you've said and what we heard from the priest in Karawa, that people can cross between different planes. I mean, there's that there's a way in which people are doorways across those different planes.
Seeker: People are doorways, and I remember that well.
Wellby: That—that if there's a different world that's the world of dreams, right? Isn't this what the what the person in Karawa was saying? Someone was telling us this.
Wellby: Couldn't they cross between these different worlds?
Seeker: I mean, this is what, this is what I'm after, Wellby. I want to cross between worlds. I've had a glimpse of it.

before: Seeker: I believe it was mentioned by the centaurs. Is that true?
DM: Yes, but literal or metaphorical, they were somewhat unclear on.
Wellby: Well, I—well, this is a good in-game conversation because like Wellby definitely interpreted like super metaphorically, which may not be true, but—

Seeker: What it means for there to be a tether between worlds—I mean, I'm especially interested in that question, and I'm making these goggles to try to see one aspect of what connects the worlds: the ley lines. We don't know why they're connected to each other in this way, and how, in general, worlds might be connected to each other, permanently or temporarily.
DM: I sent you a message.
after: Delwath: So—

Kenzo: One memory that I have that may be relevant: when we killed that demon, I remember seeing this this dark energy that was kind of spooling off of the aura of that demon, drifting off someplace else, almost as though there was that connection that that demon did have with whatever other plane we may be dealing with.
Seeker: A tether that was broken.
Unknown: [garbled].

Seeker: And so the tether is a little like the rope you put around yourself to rappel down into a canyon. But in crossing between planes, it's something that connects a person or a being in traveling between them.

review.reason: The source is an uncertain recollection; the retained question preserves the speakers’ doubt about who taught them.

interactions.title: Vola defends the Society and its search for knowledge
lines: DM: ((Dinner description)) And and as you are sitting and and eating—after dinner, let's try that—Vola turns to you and says, “Look, I know that you don't completely trust me. I get it. I don't completely trust you either. But we've been through some times together, I think, and whatever you think of me, I swear this damn Agata creature, whoever, whatever she is, is much worse than even the worst you could think of me.”

DM: You might think the Society's greedy or wrong or, you know, maybe we’re maybe we're a bit ambitious in what we're doing. But think about the alternative. Letting Agata, whatever she is, whatever they are, get their hands on all of this hidden knowledge? Fucking waste at best and a ruinous house-of-cards disaster at worst.
DM: I think you know, we could work together. I think Chardon and Dunmar and even the dwarves don't have to be enemies in this.

DM: “And I have to say, what is the point of hidden magical knowledge scattered in ruins, sitting there to rot? Think about how much knowledge has been lost time and time and time and time again throughout the history of humanity. Every time we think we're getting somewhere, disaster, calamity, and so much of this new knowledge is lost. It fucking sucks. And we can do better. And I don't know, even if it doesn't matter to all you haughty elder races, at least consider that the Society would do less harm and more good with all of this stuff that might be hidden out there than Agata.”
Seeker: In, in what way does the Society intend to do good with all this knowledge? To share with everyone?
Kenzo: Isn't that exactly the opposite of what the Society does?

DM: The Society—well, okay, everyone is maybe an exaggeration. We are a library. We preserve knowledge. Not all knowledge is safe for everybody, right? I won't say I'm the person who's making the you know the best decisions about what to do, but look, there's bad stuff out there. I think you can see that now. We can all see that. And at least the Society, we're fucking humans. We're not trying to murder innocent civilians across Dunmar. We're not you know transforming animals into rampaging beasts and sending them, God knows why, to attack who knows who. Could be a lot worse.
Seeker: Who's in charge of this Society?

DM: Don't have a name for a—well, but it is part of the—of the Great Library. Just run by the archivists. I am, I am not a high-ranking member of this group. I can't really tell you too much about leadership. All I can say is that—

DM: Word came that we needed to search for artifacts, and it's not just in Dunmar. There's groups that have been hired in and are investigating artifacts at ruins in the north, far north of Chardon. I think there's there's even people that might be heading into the blasted ruins of the of the mountains where, you know, the great calamities hundreds of years ago up ended the earth. It's—

Kenzo: The Library—how long has the Library been on this quest? This—or at least kind of accelerated this whole—what does the Library know? They know something about what's going on? That—why there—why they're trying to get these items?
DM: “I had never heard of Agata Dustmother before. I have no bloody clue what the Society knows about Agata.”
Kenzo: Agata is what's—what do you think it's a relationship with these treasure hunters and then all that crazy shit that we just saw, like that he's done, everything else?

DM: “I don't know why this creature wants to find lost knowledge on the plains, but I don't think it can be for a good purpose. The connection between what we just saw—I mean, I have to say, that orc talked like he was in charge of the place.”
Kenzo: Which orc? When we met one—
DM: Jackalweres. There was an orc and two jackalweres who were her captors, Vola's captors.
Seeker: Do you know about any recent activity of mind flayers?

DM: Recent activity? No. I heard a story about—so there's a rumor that during the Blood Years, one of the wars far to the north, there was some mind flayers that had somehow figured out how to make a mountain walk. Don't know whatever happened to that, but I guess it never got to civilization.
Seeker: Thank goodness for that. Well, I—
Kenzo: The first part—why, why is, why is the Great Library suddenly so deploying people like you all around? What, what, what, what happened that caused the Library so alarmed?
DM: “Something must have happened five, six years ago. If anything happened, I don't know what.”
Wellby: That's when they started sending groups out?
DM: That's when—I mean, it's the Library. They've always been interested in knowledge. Ever since I've been, you know, a part of the Society and and working for the Library.
Wellby: What were you before you became part of the Society?
DM: That's the kind of personal question. What were you before you came here?
Wellby: Wellby just keeps a long level silent gaze on her.

before: Kenzo: And so what is Vola cooking again?
DM: Roast chicken.
Kenzo: Oh yes. Oh, it's one of the better things we've eaten in a long time.
Unknown: Yes.
Kenzo: Oh yes, very exciting. Kenzo's very excited to eat something a little more nourishing then whatever the hell we've been eating, what other—whatever rations we've eaten.
after: Kenzo: But I think—now, I agree that relative to whatever fucking demons from hell are there, we'd like to share a common enemy and the like to share common interest in dealing with whatever the fuck that is, understanding whatever the fuck that is. Which, by the way, the Library knows something, you've shared your knowledge to the other—you know, us—maybe that would be an interesting thing to learn. I don't know if we can learn. What is your plan? Where were you kind of headed?
DM: “I'm heading back to Chardon as fast as I can. I—”
Wellby: With us to the storm first?
Seeker: Is it on the way?
Wellby: It's not not on the way.

Seeker: So you're saying Agata, like the Society, is interested in Drankorian and Dunmari—
DM: That seems to be the situation. Yes.

DM: Well, I had heard rumors. That it—there’s—there were stories that it had been the lair of a great beast, a multi headed chimera that perhaps had gathered treasure. And I—you have taken all the treasure that was possibly the the lair of this beast, and it seems there's little I can do about that.
DM: But that was my goal. Did not have designs, or knowledge rather, of your hidden dwarven artifacts.

lines: Delwath: It would be an interesting. Actually, I'm curious as to her reaction to find out that we destroy—I'll tell her. I'll ask her if she's heard anything. Have you heard any rumors of a more treasures in the desert west of Gomat—east of Gomat? She heard anything about the desert?

Delwath: Was he chasing anything in particular?
DM: Not that I know of.
Delwath: We did find a staff there.
Delwath: It's quite dark. To—dark in its purpose and intent. An artifact of Cha'mutte.
DM: “That seems dangerous. What did you do with that?”
Delwath: What would you have done with it?

DM: This is part of why the Library exists. Not all knowledge is safe. Not all powers can be used without consequence. before: Riswynn: We met somebody in that—he was—that I didn't know if he talked about it. I'm not—
